title: Point sections comparisons and coefficient-dual domains
statement:
Fix the Poincare coefficient conventions [def-pod-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Write $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$ and $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. Use the point categories and $F_\Lambda=\operatorname{Fib}_s$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], and derived tensor and internal Hom [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Let $Q_s$ be finite reduction $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ with $1\le m\le n$, integral reduction $\mathcal O_E\to A_{E,n}$, completed integral scalar extension for a finite coefficient-field extension, rationalization, or extension at a common finite coefficient-field stage. Write $\Lambda'$ for its target coefficient ring and $q$ for the corresponding coefficient-module functor.
For $B\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$ there is a natural isomorphism in $D(\Lambda')$
$$t_{Q,B}:q(F_\Lambda B)\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\Lambda'}(Q_sB).$$
For finite reduction this is the canonical balanced sections map
$$\Gamma(s,B)\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}\longrightarrow\Gamma(s,B\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}(A_{E,m})_s).$$
This finite-reduction assertion holds for every unbounded ambient complex $B$ of $(A_{E,n})_s$-modules, with its target $A_{E,m}$-module action, without requiring finite Tor amplitude of $A_{E,m}$ over $A_{E,n}$. Its inverse is the ringed-point derived-tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], using the identity-adjunction geometric point whose inverse image is final-object sections and whose coefficient ring map is the identity, as in [lem-sf-point-ringed-evaluation-model]. At integral reduction $t$ is the sections/derived-reduction map [lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction]. At integral scalar extension it is exactly $\varphi^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension], including the completion comparison, and at common field stages it is that map rationalized. At rationalization it is the identity under the defining formula for $F_E$. These specified maps respect the fibre tensor and unit constraints [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor].
For $C\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$ put $D_sC=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\omega_{s,\Lambda})$, where $u_\Lambda:\omega_{s,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_s$ is the identity-adjunction normalization [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex]. Then $D_sC$, $Q_sC$ and $D_s(Q_sC)$ belong to their corresponding bounded constructible finite-Tor categories. The canonical comparison $\delta_{Q,C}:Q_sD_sC\to D_sQ_sC$ is therefore defined on these domains; it is the transpose of coefficient-changed evaluation with $Q_s\omega_{s,\Lambda}\cong\omega_{s,\Lambda'}$, normalized by $u_{\Lambda'}$ to $Q_su_\Lambda$.

proof.text: Put $A=A_{E,n}$ and $A'=A_{E,m}$. The point of [lem-sf-point-ringed-evaluation-model] has exact inverse image $\Gamma_s$ and identity coefficient map; it takes $A_s\to A'_s$ to $A\to A'$. Its scalar square identifies the canonical sections map with the inverse of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], applied to $B$ and $A'_s$, after forgetting to $D(A)$. Thus that underlying map is invertible for every unbounded $B$. We also verify its target action. Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to B$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Its sections are K-flat by the evaluation-model statement. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] the scalar changes are represented by $\Gamma_sP\otimes_A A'$ and $P\otimes_{A_s}A'_s$. The canonical scalar comparison of the evaluation model is a morphism between these computations in $D(A')$; its balanced section rule is $A'$-linear, and the cited statements make it independent of $P$. Forgetting an $A'$-module complex to an $A$-module complex is exact and reflects zero modules, so cohomology of its cone vanishes if and only if it vanishes before forgetting. By [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology], invertibility of the underlying map therefore proves invertibility in $D(A')$. Its inverse, after forgetting, is precisely the ringed-point derived-tensor comparison, with the target action just verified. This proves the stated ambient $t_{Q,B}$ and its naturality, without any finite Tor amplitude or K-flatness assumption on $A'$ over $A$.

proof.text: For integral reduction, apply [lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction] to $B$: it is an integral bounded constructible object because it belongs to the stated finite-Tor subcategory. This gives the specified natural map $\Gamma(s,B)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\to\Gamma(s,B\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})$ as an isomorphism in $D(A_{E,n})$. For a finite field extension $E\subset L$, apply [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] to the integral object $B$ and define $t_{Q,B}=\varphi_{L/E,B}^{-1}$. Its stated formula is exactly $\Gamma(s,\chi_{L/E,B})\circ\theta_{L/E,B}$, so this includes the specified completion comparison rather than substituting an ordinary uncompleted scalar functor. Both results assert naturality in the derived object.

source.place: Second paragraph: coefficient passage; integral reduction and completed integral scalar extension

proof.text: At rationalization, [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] defines $F_E$ on objects as $\Gamma(s,B)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ and on arrows by scalar linear extension. Thus both sides of $t$ are this same functor and $t$ is the identity. At a common finite field stage use the rationalized isomorphism of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension], inverted in the same direction as in Step 2. Its identity and tower equalities imply that enlargement of the common stage gives the same comparison: the two routes are the two sides of that tower equality, with the intermediate $\varphi$ and its inverse cancelled. This is exactly the representative rule defining $F_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$ in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], so it is natural for common-stage morphisms. Finally [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor] states compatibility of its tensor and unit constraints with finite reduction and scalar extension in these coefficient constructions. Together with the scalar square of [lem-sf-point-ringed-evaluation-model] for Step 1, it gives the asserted tensor and unit compatibility of the specified maps at every stage.

source.place: Second paragraph: coefficient passage, tensor and unit constraints, rational and common-stage comparisons

proof.text: We check the finite-quotient domain without requiring the quotient ring to have finite Tor dimension. If $C$ has Tor interval $[a,b]$, [lem-sf-point-tor-amplitude-realization] supplies a finite free $A$-complex $P$ supported in $[a,b]$ representing $F_A C$. By [lem-pod-point-exact-extension-sections], the extension functor $L_A$ and sections are exact, have the explicit adjunction there, and have coefficient ring $\Gamma_s A_s=A$. Hence the hypotheses of [lem-pod-point-sections-reconstruction] hold, and its actual counit identifies $L_A P$ with $C$. A term of $L_A P$ is a finite sum of $A_s$; changing coefficients sends it to the same finite sum of $A'_s$, with the differential matrix reduced modulo $\varpi_E^m$. This bounded free sheaf complex is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. The computation of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] therefore represents $Q_sC$ by its termwise scalar change. The coefficient unit is constructible by [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible] and has Tor interval $[0,0]$ since it is the tensor unit. Taking the finite sequence of shifts and cones of its terms, [lem-weil-finite-ctf-triangulated] shows that $Q_sC$ is bounded constructible finite-Tor. Equivalently its free complex already gives the interval $[a,b]$ on tensoring with any degree-zero $A'_s$-module.

source.place: Second paragraph: finite-Tor coefficient domains; bounded free point models and quotient coefficients

proof.text: For integral reduction, bounded constructibility of $Q_sC$ is part of the integral category in [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]; its finite Tor interval is one of the uniform reduction intervals required by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. For completed integral scalar extension, [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible] puts $Q_sC$ in the target integral bounded constructible category, and [thm-sf-ctf-stability] states that this category equals its finite-Tor subcategory. Rationalization and finite field extension are functors between the bounded constructible categories by [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Such objects are finite-Tor by the field-stage definition in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. The same holds for objects represented at a common finite coefficient-field stage by [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. This verifies $Q_sC$ belongs to the claimed domain for every remaining $Q$.

source.place: Second paragraph: integral, rational and common-stage coefficient domains

proof.text: The point $s$ is a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, its structure map being the identity. Apply the Verdier-duality preservation of [thm-sf-ctf-stability], clause (vi), to $C$ at a finite stage. It gives $D_sC\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$. The integral and field conclusions of the same statement give this at $\mathcal O_E$, $E$ and $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Apply it again at the target coefficient stage to $Q_sC$, whose membership was proved in Steps 4 and 5. This gives $D_s(Q_sC)$ in the target finite-Tor category. In particular $t_{Q,D_sC}$ is also on its asserted bounded finite-Tor domain. The normalization [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex] identifies the dualizing object of this identity structure morphism with the coefficient unit, so these are exactly the $D_s$ functors in the statement.

source.place: Second paragraph: point duals and their bounded finite-Tor domains

proof.text:
Write $e_Q:Q_s\Lambda_s\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda'_s$ for the coefficient-unit identification. It is the scalar unit identification at finite reduction and is preserved by the completed and field-stage coefficient comparisons of [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. Using $u$ from [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex], set
$$w_Q=u_{\Lambda'}^{-1}\circ e_Q\circ Q_su_\Lambda:Q_s\omega_{s,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{s,\Lambda'}.$$
Thus $u_{\Lambda'}\circ w_Q=e_Q\circ Q_su_\Lambda$, precisely the required normalization. Apply $Q_s$ to evaluation $D_sC\otimes^L C\to\omega_{s,\Lambda}$, precede it by the inverse coefficient-tensor comparison, and follow it by $w_Q$. The tensor comparison exists for finite reduction by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and for the completed and field coefficient constructions by [lem-fix-operation-reduction]. This gives the actual arrow
$$Q_sD_sC\otimes^L Q_sC\longrightarrow Q_s\omega_{s,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{w_Q}\omega_{s,\Lambda'}.$$
By [thm-sf-ctf-stability], clause (vii), the canonical internal-Hom coefficient comparison on these finite-Tor domains exists and preserves evaluation. Compose that comparison with $R\mathcal Hom_s(1,w_Q)$. Its evaluation is the displayed arrow, so this is precisely the canonical evaluation transpose $\delta_{Q,C}:Q_sD_sC\to R\mathcal Hom_s(Q_sC,\omega_{s,\Lambda'})=D_sQ_sC$. Steps 4--6, also applied to $D_sC$, put both endpoints in their claimed categories. This proves existence and the specified normalization; no invertibility of $\delta$ is needed here.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NF-ac4ad46b4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, all 23 cited statements and the source paragraph (main-20261015 thm-pod-global-verdier-duality.proof.md, second paragraph). No new nodes, the inherited Q14 statement is kept, there is no SGA citation and no cycle. Step 1: the unbounded finite reduction holds via the ringed-topos tensor-pullback lemma for arbitrary G (A'_s is not flat, which the step handles correctly). The target A'-action is shown by a K-flat resolution plus derived change of rings, and invertibility lifts to D(A') by the cohomology criterion. Step 2: the derived-reduction lemma applies verbatim, and t = phi^{-1} = Gamma(chi) o theta has the right direction. Step 3: rationalization is the identity by the definition of F_E; the common stage follows from the tower equality. Step 4: the finite free model, the reconstruction counit (its hypotheses are exactly lem-pod-point-exact-extension-sections), bounded flat implies K-flat, and the cone/shift closure give Q_sC in D^b_ctf over A'. Step 5: the remaining Q follow from the integral definition, scalar-extension constructibility plus ctf-stability (vii), and the field-stage definitions. Step 6: ctf-stability (vi)/(vii) at s = Spec k. Step 7: w_Q is normalized by construction and delta is the evaluation transpose; only existence is claimed. Small cases C = unit, n = m, rank-one shift and the nonflat Z/l^2 -> Z/l edge case are consistent. The 14 tool_uses are accepted as generic black boxes; their 'why' text is boilerplate. Batch-5 finding (reconstruction reaches lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction): not a fault. That lemma is a generic point coefficient lemma from prop-cohomological-finiteness that neither assumption gives, it is already a stmt_dep of the item on base, and the item itself lies inside the proof of thm-pod-global-verdier-duality, so it cannot cite nt-assume-poincare-duality.
